newsitem.title: PANAMA: Ecuador's deposed leader pens autobiography.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's deposed leader pens autobiography.

text.p: Ecuador's deposed president Abdala Bucaram has written a "kiss and tell" autobiography which should hit Latin American book stores later this month, he said.

Called "The Fox Plan: To Kill Bucaram," the former leader, who continues to call himself president, told reporters late on Friday that the book recounts how he was deposed by Congress in February on grounds of "mental incompetence" after only six months in office.
"I am the plan, meaning, the coup d'etat. It also talks about the attempts to kill me," said Bucaram, who treated the national and international media to a party in a bar in the capital city.

"I wrote the book, it's finished. It should be out by the end of the month. It is kiss and tell, but there is also political reflection," he said, adding that he is in talks with a Latin American publishing house.

Bucaram, known as "el loco" (the crazy one) for his eccentric personal style, said he included in the chapters episodes from his previous exile in Panama from 1985-90 when he fled charges of corruption as mayor of his home city, Guayaquil.
"During my first exile on Sept. 15, 1985, I used a disguise as a woman and I changed my name. When the paramilitaries came to look for me the next day in the hotel, no one knew," he said.
Panama recently granted political asylum to Bucaram, his wife, four children and brother Sanitago who was expelled from Ecuador's Congress.

Ecuador's Supreme Court has issued a warrant for Bucaram's arrest on grounds of misuse of presidential funds. Congress has expelled 13 deputies, including his brother, who was accused of siphoning funds from the national budget.
